body: Novo pioneered GLP-1s (Victoza 2010, Ozempic 2017, Wegovy for obesity June 2021). Rise: STEP-1 (Feb 2021, ~15% weight loss), Wegovy launch June 2021 with supply shortages for two years, SELECT (Aug 2023, ~20% fewer heart events). The stock roughly quadrupled from 2021 [approx] and Novo became Europe's most valuable company, worth >$600-650bn at the June 2024 peak — more than Denmark's GDP; ADR ~$145-150 (2:1 split Sep 2023) [unverified]. Mostly EPS growth (sales/EPS growing 20-30%+), with P/E expanding to ~40-45x [unverified]. Reversal: Dec 20 2024 CagriSema trial disappointment -20% (record one-day fall); Lilly's tirzepatide took 63% of US branded obesity scripts by Q3 2025; compounded semaglutide eroded cash pay; CEO Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen ousted May 16 2025 (shares -59% from June 2024 high at that point); new CEO Mike Doustdar cut 9,000 jobs (Sept 2025); Nov 2025 US pricing deal cut government prices; 2026 guidance: first sales decline in modern history (-5% to -13%); Feb 23 2026 CagriSema lost head-to-head vs tirzepatide, -16%, shares at lowest since June 2021 — ~$475bn (~73%) wiped. EARLY SIGNAL (up): Wegovy shortages = demand exceeding supply for 2+ years. EARLY SIGNAL (down): SURPASS/SURMOUNT data showing a better competitor molecule plus Lilly out-investing in capacity, and Novo's next-gen data underwhelming in Dec 2024. LESSON: the category creator does not automatically own the category; peak valuation coincided with peak scarcity, and a superior fast follower plus price normalisation erased the whole Wegovy-era gain.

data.early_signals: up: Wegovy shortages; down: Lilly superior data, CagriSema miss Dec 2024
data.eps_vs_rerating: up: EPS + P/E to ~40x; down: P/E collapse + EPS cuts
data.lesson: category creator lost to faster follower; peak scarcity = peak price
data.who_caught_it: broad European/US growth funds; no documented single name

title: Novo Nordisk 2016-2026: GLP-1 category creator, round trip -73%

body: Sensex ~2,900 (April 2003) to 21,206.77 (10 Jan 2008), about 7x in under five years. Drivers: GDP growth 8-9%, ~30% credit growth, a corporate capex boom, a global commodity super-cycle and record FII inflows. Leaders: real estate (DLF IPO July 2007, then India's largest; Unitech), infrastructure developers and power (GMR, GVK, Lanco, Reliance Power), capital goods (BHEL, L&T, Suzlon), metals. Laggards: IT (after 2000), FMCG and pharma - defensives looked 'boring'. Valuation at peak: Sensex trailing P/E ~27-28x; market cap/GDP widely cited near 150% (one Business Standard figure is dated 'Dec 2017', likely meaning 2007). Top signals visible at the time: Reliance Power's Jan 2008 IPO (~Rs 11,560 crore, oversubscribed ~70x, listed below its issue price on 11 Feb 2008 - detail from memory), Sensex 10k to 20k in ~2 years, mid/small caps outrunning large caps, infra companies valued on land banks and order books rather than cash flows, rising leverage. What followed: a ~61% Sensex crash; the Indian capital goods index needed until ~2021 to regain its 2007-08 peak; Nifty Realty remains far below its 2008 high (unverified current level). Lesson: a capex-and-credit boom produces the biggest losses in the sectors that led it; land-bank and order-book valuations are reflexive.

data.early_signals: RPower IPO frenzy, leverage, land-bank valuations
data.lesson: leaders of a capex boom lose most

body: After falling −99.6% from 2008 (see case_study:suzlon), the price went from ₹1.70 (Mar 2020) → ₹83.5 (Sep 2024) ≈49x. P/E is not meaningful because EPS was negative until FY23; the engine was balance-sheet repair. Steps: a 2020 lender restructuring; an Oct 2022 rights issue of ₹1,200 cr at ₹5/share (1.8x subscribed, ~₹600 cr to debt); an Aug 2023 QIP that took the company to net cash of ₹599 cr (Sep 2023) from net debt of ₹1,180 cr (Mar 2023). The share count rose heavily (exact figure unverified). Most of the move came in 2023 (₹10 → ₹38). Revenue FY21 ₹3,346 cr → FY26 ₹16,732 cr; OPM 16–18%; FY26 PAT ₹3,163 cr included a ₹718 cr tax write-back. Early signal: an offer to all shareholders at ₹5 with the founder family participating, order inflows (C&I, hybrid), and the net-cash milestone, all in exchange filings. Ended/stalled: −59% to ₹33.9 (Oct 2026); Q2 FY27 PAT −69% YoY against the tax-boosted base, flat EBITDA with lower margin, the EPC share of the order book rising to 38%; order book still >6 GW. P/E ~22 now. Lesson: distressed-equity repair can 50x a near-dead stock, but once it is clean it rerates to a normal multiple and becomes an execution and margin story.

data.early_signals: 2022 rights at ₹5; 2023 QIP; net cash Sep 2023
